title: Job-to-data versus data-to-job placement evidence
summary: Storage publishes locality and movement evidence to Job-to-Node Allocation so the planner can compare moving a small job to existing data with moving large data to a job. Storage does not own hard node eligibility or the final placement lease.
invariants: Hard security, legal, access, runtime/software and hardware eligibility is evaluated before locality can improve ranking.
Locality is an optimization, not permission.
Candidate evidence includes input bytes, local input bytes, materialisation bytes, job-package bytes, workspace feasibility and mandatory output export.
Expected output movement matters: a job with small input and huge output may prefer a different location than input-only reasoning suggests.
Disposable workspace adds mandatory output-commit movement because its result cannot count as durably complete in place.
Storage classifications JOB_TO_DATA, DATA_TO_JOB, MIXED and INFEASIBLE are descriptive storage evidence; Job-to-Node remains placement authority.
Fleet assessment emits evidence for every known node rather than silently choosing a winner.
Unqualified devices and unknown node capacity are excluded from storage feasibility until explicitly admitted/observed.

provenance.claim: Regression proves job-to-data/data-to-job movement evidence, separate node capacity and mandatory output export from disposable workspace.
Regression proves ED209 fleet matrix semantics and no invented/unqualified capacity.
